A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HARP research. All pages, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison; retained content can be matched across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, pruning and rescaling ablations, calibration experiments, and repeated inference-time measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including generation, discriminative, LongBench, ablation, and efficiency evaluations.

M1.justification: Both versions prune higher-layer query/key projections, retain value/output projections, and select rescaling parameters through the same top-down greedy procedure in Algorithm 1. Expanded explanations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same five short-context generation benchmarks, six discriminative benchmarks, and 16 LongBench datasets, and use WikiText and Pile10K for calibration analyses. Multimodal evaluation appears only as future work in v2.

E2.justification: The evaluated Mag-sp, Wanda-sp, FLAP, and LLM-Pruner comparisons are unchanged, including LLM-Pruner's restriction to LLaMA3.1-8B. V2's new Table 1 summarizes existing methods without introducing an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The model settings, pruning ratios, benchmark protocols, metrics, and tuned layer ranges match. However, v2's new cost paragraph specifies 10 rescaling candidates, while Algorithm 1 retains the 11-value grid from 0 to 1 in increments of 0.1. It is unclear whether the search budget changed or the new count is erroneous.

E4.justification: V2 adds an analytical comparison of HARP's search overhead against single-pass pruning baselines in Section 3.1. The existing layer-selection, rescaling, calibration-corpus, and sequence-length analyses remain unchanged; no additional measured timing experiment accompanies this comparison.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 repetitions and 95% confidence intervals for inference timing in Section 3.6. No new seed information, uncertainty-reporting practice, or statistical test is introduced.

E6.justification: The corresponding benchmark and ablation tables, searched rescaling values, perplexities, and timing results are unchanged. V2 newly reports analytical estimates of 80 search passes and approximately 80 times single-pass baseline calibration cost. These are added cost estimates, not measured performance improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds a substantial proof for v1's Proposition 2, now Proposition 1, introducing reasoning about norm preservation for all inputs and orthogonality. Theorem 1 gains an explicit converse asserting non-uniform attention when similarity stays below one. Section 2.1 also corrects the dominant attention-complexity expression from O(Nd²) to O(N²d).

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same method and performance contributions. The revised conclusion additionally claims practical deployment benefits for resource-constrained and interactive applications, explicitly stating that architectural changes are unnecessary.

C2.justification: V2 adds search-cost amortization reasoning and describes comparison against tuned baselines as conservative. It replaces Appendix E with different limitations and future directions in the conclusion, dropping the explicit call to recover mathematical-task performance. Model-dependent rescaling remains discussed in Section 3.5.

D1.justification: V2 adds a HARP code-access link, baseline-metric documentation, and search-cost accounting. It removes v1's explicit instruction for replicating value representations under grouped-query attention. Hardware, evaluation-harness version, and tuned pruning ranges remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 removes the GQA reference by Ainslie et al. and the zeroth-order optimization references by Guo et al. and Zhang et al., alongside their associated discussions. The remaining cited works and the broad related-work positioning are retained.

P1.justification: V2 expands selected method and theory explanations, rewrites the conclusion, and edits appendix explanations while preserving the main section order and much of the experimental prose. It also adopts author-year citations and publication headers.

P2.justification: The journal template substantially reformats the presentation. Algorithm 1 and Figures 2–3 become larger standalone displays instead of text-wrapped elements, a qualitative method-comparison table is added, and captions and table emphasis are revised. The existing empirical displays retain their underlying results.

improvement.justification: V2 improves visual readability and adds a code link and cost documentation while retaining the empirical evidence. However, the added Proposition 1 proof incorrectly treats one-hot rows as necessarily forming a permutation, and the new 80-pass estimate conflicts with the retained 11-candidate grid. Together with the removed GQA implementation detail and explicit mathematical-task limitation, these tradeoffs prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
